chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti from Hammad b. Uthman from Abdullah b. Abi Ya'fur from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

The Messenger of God (blessings be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon to the people in his Farewell Pilgrimage in Mina in the Mosque of Khayf. He praised God and commended Him, then said: May God grant joy to a servant who heard my sayings and understood them, then delivers them to those who did not hear them. For there may be a carrier of knowledge who is not a person of understanding, and there may be a carrier of knowledge who brings it to one who is more knowledgeable than him. Three things do not cause the heart of a Muslim to feel trouble: sincerity in deeds for God, wishing well for the Imams of the Muslims, and sticking to their community. For their supplications encompass those behind them. The Muslims are brethren: their blood is equivalent, and the lowest of them strives to protect them. They are one hand against those who oppose them.

key_terms.النصيحة لأئمة المسلمين: Sincere counsel to the leaders/Imams of the Muslims
key_terms.تتكافأ دماؤهم: Their blood is equivalent; a principle of Muslim equality
key_terms.حجة الوداع: Farewell Pilgrimage; the Prophet's final pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.مسجد الخيف: Mosque of Khayf; a mosque in Mina where the Prophet delivered this sermon

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say in his Farewell Pilgrimage sermon at the Mosque of Khayf?
ai.summary: In his Farewell Pilgrimage at the Mosque of Khayf in Mina, the Prophet Muhammad (s) delivers a sermon with three timeless directives that define authentic Muslim communal life. He begins by invoking God's blessing upon those who hear, preserve, and transmit his words, acknowledging that a carrier of knowledge may not fully comprehend it and may convey it to someone more qualified. He then identifies three principles that keep a Muslim's heart free from rancor: sincerity in worship for God alone, sincere counsel to the Imams (leaders) of the Muslims, and commitment to the Muslim community. He concludes with a declaration of Muslim brotherhood -- their blood is equivalent, even the lowliest among them is honored, and they stand united against all opposition.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti from Hammad b. `Uthman from `Abdullah b. Abi Ya`fur from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) delivered a sermon to the people in his Farewell Pilgrimage in Mina in the Mosque of Khayf. So, he praised Allah and commended Him. Then, he said: May Allah grant joy to a servant who heard my sayings and understood them, then delivers them to those who did not hear them. There can be a carrier of knowledge who is not a person of understanding, and there could be a carrier of knowledge who brings it to one who is more knowledgeable than him. There are three things that the heart of a Muslim person does not feel trouble in: (1) sincerity in deeds for Allah, (2) wishing well for the Imams of the Muslims, and (3) sticking to their community (jama`a), for their supplications encompass those behind them. The Muslims are brethren: their blood is equivalent, and [even] the lowest of them strives to protect them. They are [one] hand against those who oppose them.
